title: The tagged molecule
hook: The mix stays at 50 A and 50 B. Has the reaction stopped?

knows: that some reactions can run both ways (A can become B and B can become A)
that a reaction changes one kind of molecule into another
doesNotKnow: that at equilibrium both directions keep running
that steady totals can hide constant change

misconception: At equilibrium the reaction has stopped: nothing is changing any more.
objective: The learner can explain that equilibrium is steady counts produced by two-way traffic at equal rates: individual molecules keep changing type while the totals hold.

claims.text: At chemical equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so the amounts stay constant while individual molecules keep reacting (dynamic equilibrium).
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'chemical equilibrium' (reversible process ultimately reaching a point where the rates in both directions are identical); Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry (dynamic equilibrium); isotope-exchange experiments show the continuing traffic.

claims.text: In this model each tick 12 A become B and 12 B become A, about a quarter of the 100 molecules, so the counts stay at 50 and 50.
claims.source: Simulation rule (seeded): 12 + 12 = 24 of 100 change per tick; net change 12 - 12 = 0. Each molecule has a 12/50 = 24% chance to change per tick.

claims.text: The simulation is a model: it forces exactly equal traffic each tick, while real mixtures balance on average and their counts jitter slightly.
claims.source: Modelling simplification stated in the reveal. In a real system k_f[A] = k_b[B] holds for the average rates; fluctuations in counts scale roughly as the square root of the number of molecules (any statistical-mechanics text).

claims.text: The reveal's count of how many times the tagged molecules changed type is read from the learner's own run, and covers only the ticks each molecule was followed since it was tagged.
claims.source: Counted from the stored history of each tagged molecule (number of adjacent ticks where its type differs). | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Stage sentence reported changes over the lesson's total ticks even for a molecule tagged later. Demo.tsx now prints 'in the N ticks you followed it' (single tag) or 'in total while you followed them' (several), using each tag's history length.

recall.question: A sealed flask has held the same amounts of A and B for an hour. What is happening inside?
options: A→B and B→A both continue at equal rates
recall.why: Equilibrium is two-way traffic at equal rates. The totals are steady because the changes balance, not because they stop.
